reviews.basis: Player_AnimationFrameTable selects this sprite mapping at the stated index after masking the animation accumulator to eight entries.
reviews.reason: Player_AdvanceAnimationFrame masks the accumulator with $1C and indexes the eight longwords of Player_AnimationFrameTable. Its slots 0 through 7 point in order to these eight mapping labels. The identical sentence states only that shared table relationship; it does not infer the appearance of any frame.

reviews.basis: A SharedCombatSpriteAnimation stream names this frame via a signed relative offset; Anim_ResolveTimedMappingFrame adds that offset to the cursor, and Sprite_RenderObjectList passes the result to Sprite_RenderMapping on its draw path. The suffix records ROM order, not visual identity.
reviews.reason: Each of these 69 mappings occurs as a dc.w Frame-* relative target in src/data/shared_combat_sprite_animations.s. Anim_ResolveTimedMappingFrame adds the signed offset at (a4) to its cursor; the ordinary Sprite_RenderObjectList draw path then calls Sprite_RenderMapping. The three Stage 15 fragment mappings are excluded and have separate evidence.

reviews.basis: Anim_ResolveTimedMappingFrame reads this ROM-ordered stream as pairs of signed relative mapping offsets and timing or control words; the numeric suffix denotes ROM order, not a visual identity.
reviews.reason: Each of these 33 ROM-ordered animation labels starts with a relative SharedCombatSpriteFrame pointer followed by a timing word. Anim_ResolveTimedMappingFrame reads the paired words, advances by four bytes between records, and follows a relative sequence pointer when the timing word is zero. The former index 30 has its own Counter Force name and is not part of this group.

reviews.basis: The eight-direction SevenForcesRotationFrameTable0 through SevenForcesRotationFrameTable8 pointer sets select this sprite mapping record. The suffix preserves ROM order without assigning a specific form or body part.
reviews.reason: The nine labelled SevenForcesRotationFrameTable0..8 bases collectively contain pointers to all 40 listed mapping labels. Sprite_ApplyMetaspriteEightFrameRotation masks its table offset with $1C, selecting one of eight slots from a descriptor base. Table1 is followed by a second unlabelled eight-pointer run before Table2; the Table1 base cannot select that run with this mask, and no wider reachability is claimed.

reviews.basis: Named Enemy_Projectile animation streams select this sprite mapping; the numeric suffix preserves ROM order without guessing a pose.
reviews.reason: Every listed mapping appears as a dc.w Enemy_ProjectileSpriteMappingNN-* target in one of the ten Enemy_ProjectileAnimation00..09 streams. Anim_UpdateProjectileAnimation selects those streams through Enemy_ProjectileAnimationPointers, and the mapping names claim only ROM order rather than a visual pose. No frame-to-pose identity is inferred.

reviews.basis: Boss_Shellshogun pointer tables or direct assignments select this sprite mapping; the numeric suffix preserves ROM order without guessing a visual pose.
reviews.reason: Six eight-entry Boss_ShellshogunRotationFramesA..F tables select mappings 03..26. The metasprite descriptor directly names mappings 00 and 02, body-frame assignments name 00 and 01, and Boss_ShellshogunRotatingPartFrameTable names 27..29. These static sources account for every listed mapping; numeric suffixes preserve ROM order and do not assert a visual pose.

reviews.basis: WeaponSetup_ControlTypeTextPointers selects this encoded string at the matching TYPE 1--26 display index.
reviews.reason: WeaponSetup_ControlTypeTextPointers contains exactly 26 longwords in label order 01..26. WeaponSetup_RenderSelectedControlType scales WeaponSetupControlIndex by four and reads that table entry. The eight-byte strings share the TYPE prefix and encode the matching decimal index with digit bytes 1=0 through A=9, followed by $FF; single-digit values use a zero spacer. This is a table and byte-format claim, not an inferred visual pose.

reviews.basis: The encoded glyph bytes decode to the exact weapon-setup or control-test label stated by the symbol and are consumed by the setup text renderer.
reviews.reason: These 20 definitions are dc.b text data, not executable entries. Their alphabetic glyph bytes $B..$24 encode A..Z with zero spaces, yielding the named heading, force, mode, status, exit, or control-test label; $2E precedes button glyphs where present. Every record is reached by a lea or dc.l reference in weapon_setup_screen.s, whose text paths call Text_QueueDoubleHeightStringWrapped. The two executable entries formerly sharing this sentence are excluded.

reviews.basis: A Stage 12 Teddy Bear animation stream in the same mapping bank references this high-bit-terminated sprite mapping.
reviews.reason: Each of the 18 A-R mapping labels is the target of at least one dc.w Mapping-* entry in the adjacent timed animation streams. Every mapping ends with a sprite command whose first word has bit 15 set. Anim_ResolveTimedMappingFrame adds the signed relative target to its cursor. The Stage12_TeddyBearAnimationVariant streams have no proven source caller; this review establishes table membership and record format, not runtime reachability or visual pose.

reviews.basis: One or more entries in the seven-stream Enemy_PhasePatternAnimationBySelector set stores a self-relative pointer to this high-bit-terminated sprite mapping.
reviews.reason: Enemy_ApplyPhasePatternAnimationSelector indexes the seven entries of Enemy_PhasePatternAnimationBySelector. Across those seven streams, every A-Q mapping is the target of at least one dc.w Mapping-* relative entry; each mapping's final sprite command has bit 15 set in its first word. The common sentence claims table membership and record format, not a visual pose or execution of every selector in every game state.

reviews.basis: One or more of the four streams selected by Enemy_Stage10WaspAnimationMappings stores a self-relative pointer to this high-bit-terminated sprite mapping.
reviews.reason: Enemy_UpdateStage10WaspAnimation indexes the four longwords of Enemy_Stage10WaspAnimationMappings. Across their four streams, each A-M mapping is targeted by at least one dc.w Mapping-* entry, and every mapping's final sprite command has bit 15 set in its first word. Selector0C is also assigned during defeat conversion. The shared claim establishes exact stream membership and record format, not one exclusive runtime state or a visual pose.

reviews.basis: The named Sharpssteel state or controller loads this byte stream directly into the blade pose-command interpreter.
reviews.reason: All 13 members are dc.b command streams in sharpssteel_blades.s and each is loaded into a1 by a lea in sharpssteel_core.s or sharpssteel_blades.s. The manual-control path calls Boss_SharpssteelRunBladePoseCommands directly; the other named paths enter Boss_SharpssteelUpdateBladeAssembly, which begins with that call. Each stream ends in $FF,$FF or $FF,$FE. This shared basis proves data type and interpreter connection, not the higher-level visual identity of the pose.

reviews.basis: Gfx_LoadMultiplePalettes consumes these signed words as a zero-terminated list relative to Gfx_LoadPalettePreservingSharedColor; the named stage or screen is the static pointer owner.
reviews.reason: Each of these 11 records defines one zero-terminated list of dc.w offsets relative to Gfx_LoadPalettePreservingSharedColor and has a named screen, cutscene, or stage configuration pointer in source. Gfx_LoadMultiplePalettes reads the signed word, stops at zero, extends it and adds the preserving-loader base before loading the command. ContinueScreenPaletteOffsetLists is excluded because it contains two consecutive lists and only the first has a direct source pointer; its separate address basis states that limit.

reviews.basis: The named battle-state path loads this word stream into the Valkirie pose interpreter; $80xx words publish events and $FFFE/$FFFF terminate or loop.
reviews.reason: Each of these nine named state scripts has a direct lea Script(pc),a1 in valkirie_battle.s followed by a branch or call to Entity_RenderValkirieBattleAnimation, which calls Anim_UpdateValkiriePoseScript. The streams are dc.w words and each ends in $FFFE or $FFFF; the state-4-to-8 stream also has an internal $FFFF. The three airborne variants are excluded: their addresses are first stored in field $41C(a5) and later loaded indirectly, and their former High/Mid/Low names asserted unproved visual height.

reviews.basis: The structural name records exact width and row position without inventing semantics for the overlapping users.
reviews.reason: The twelve members are longwords 1 through 6 at offsets +4 through +$18 in each of two consecutive 32-byte RAM rows. Effect_ApplyTransitionMask starts at TransitionPatternRow0 and TransitionPatternRow1, then performs two post-increment longword reads/writes per row over four DBF iterations, covering elements 0 through 7. Element 0 in each row and element 7 at each boundary have separately specific evidence; the twelve middle records share only the proven physical width and position, not one scene-specific meaning. Results and boss/cutscene code overlay the same addresses.

reviews.basis: Missiray bullet animation streams select this ROM-ordered sprite mapping record; the suffix does not guess a visual transformation stage.
reviews.reason: All eleven mapping definitions are relative dc.w Frame-* targets in the three Missiray bullet sprite-animation streams in shield_viper_and_missiray_mappings.s. Frame00 occurs in both the initial and transform streams; frames 01-04 occur in the looping stream, while frames 05-10 occur in the transform stream. Projectile_InitMissirayBullet installs the initial pointer, Projectile_MissirayBulletTransform installs the transform pointer, and Projectile_MissirayBulletWaitForTransformFrame installs the loop pointer. The shared sentence states membership and ROM-order naming only, not visual transformation stages or actual runtime reach of every frame.

reviews.basis: Named Enemy_Bird animation streams select this sprite mapping; the numeric suffix preserves ROM order without guessing a pose.
reviews.reason: All eleven mappings are relative dc.w Mapping-* targets in Enemy_BirdAnimation00 through 03. Streams 00 and 01 traverse frames 00-06 forward and backward with different delays; streams 02 and 03 use frames 07-10. The four stream pointers are entries of Enemy_BirdAnimationMappings, indexed by Enemy_UpdateBirdAnimation. Every mapping ends in a high-bit sprite command; streams 00-02 loop to themselves with zero delay and stream 03 ends with $FF. This establishes membership and structural interpretation, not visual pose identities or reachability of each selector during gameplay.

reviews.basis: Boss_SniperHoneyviperTentacleDirectionFrames selects this tentacle mapping through one of its eight indexed longword slots; the suffix records mapping ROM order, not a direction or visual pose.
reviews.reason: The sole source references to all eight mapping definitions are the eight dc.l entries of Boss_SniperHoneyviperTentacleDirectionFrames, in slot order 04/03/02/01/00/07/06/05. Boss_SniperHoneyviperUpdateTentaclesAndChainParts loads that table into a1, masks each of two angles with $E0, shifts by three to obtain byte offsets 0 through $1C, and copies the selected longword to the two tentacle part mapping fields $1E8 and $2A8. Each mapping is a one-sprite record with a high-bit first command. This proves table membership and source ownership, not visual direction names or that all eight slots are reached at runtime.

reviews.basis: Both alternating shared streams reference this high-bit-terminated sprite mapping.
reviews.reason: Both relative-offset streams in src/data/shared_stage_object_sprite_mappings.s name A, B, A, C in that order and loop. Each of the three mapping records is a single six-byte command whose first word has bit 15 set. The claim is only shared stream membership, not a visual pose identity.

reviews.basis: The streams are selected by the Stage 12 floating-object table and Gusthead debris table; the 5/4 stream is also assigned to a Sharpssteel projectile.
reviews.reason: Enemy_Stage12FloatingAnimationMappings and Boss_GustheadRandomDebrisMappings each point to both alternating streams, while Projectile_SharpssteelEmitFallingShotLoop assigns the 5/4 stream directly. Both streams contain the same A/B/A/C mapping set, with different duration words.

reviews.basis: Enemy_Stage10BeetleLoopAnimation references this high-bit-terminated sprite mapping, and both the beetle initializer and controller install that stream.
reviews.reason: The beetle stream's relative targets are A/B/A/C with duration words 2/3/2/3 and a self-loop. Enemy_Stage10BeetleInit and Enemy_Stage10BeetleController both write its address to field 8. A, B, and C are distinct six-byte high-bit-terminated mapping records, so the repeated membership statement has exact members.

reviews.basis: Weapon_UpdatePlayerFiring consumes this primary-layout table as eight signed X offsets followed by eight signed Y offsets.
reviews.reason: Each named primary variant occupies exactly eight dc.w values (16 bytes). Weapon_UpdatePlayerFiring uses the direction index in d6 to read a signed byte at (a4,d6.w) and a signed byte at 8(a4,d6.w); player render paths load each variant's address into a4. Bit 3 of $E(a5) mirrors X only. The shared sentence states this byte layout, not a pose identity.

reviews.basis: Weapon_UpdatePlayerFiring consumes this alternate-layout table as eight signed X offsets followed by eight signed Y offsets.
reviews.reason: The three repeated alternate variants are each exactly 16 bytes and are loaded into a4 by distinct armed-player render paths. The same signed-byte reads at offsets 0 and 8 apply. Variant 0 has a separately worded evidence record and is not a member of this repeated sentence; the suffixes assert table variants, not visual poses.

reviews.basis: The named Medusa state loads this word stream through lea Script(pc),a1 before Boss_RenderMedusaPose invokes Boss_UpdateMedusaPoseScript; $FFFE stops the script and $FFFF loops it.
reviews.reason: These seven dc.w command streams each have a direct lea Script(pc),a1 in a Medusa state handler, followed by a call or branch to Boss_RenderMedusaPose, which invokes Boss_UpdateMedusaPoseScript. Each stream ends in $FFFE or $FFFF. The state-A/C and state-10 scripts also have pointer stores for linked objects; the common claim does not assert exclusive direct use. Medusa_PoseFrameData is excluded: initialization stores its base in $35C(a5), and the interpreter adds script offsets to that base. Medusa_InitialPoseChannelValues already has separate evidence showing initial fixed-point values, not delays.

reviews.basis: After appending particle OAM, Player_RenderDeathParticles masks FrameCounter to $1C and selects this ROM-ordered death-sequence mapping through Player_DeathSequenceAnimationFrames for player field 8(a5).
reviews.reason: Player_RenderDeathParticles first fills a scratch OAM buffer by repeatedly calling Player_WriteDeathParticleSprite and calls Sprite_AppendOAMEntries. Only afterward does it shift FrameCounter by two, mask it with $1C, and use the resulting longword offset to write one of these eight mapping pointers into player field 8(a5). The eight dc.l entries in Player_DeathSequenceAnimationFrames point to these records in ROM order. Their art sources are referenced by the mapping records, not by the particle OAM writer; the former DeathParticle mapping/art names conflated the two paths. This review establishes static ownership and selection order, not a visually confirmed death pose.

reviews.basis: A named Sirene state loads this word command stream with lea Script(pc),a1 and enters Boss_RenderSirenePose, which calls Boss_UpdateSirenePoseScript.
reviews.reason: Sirene_State2PoseScript, Sirene_ActivePoseScript, and Sirene_State4And6PoseScript each have direct lea Script(pc),a1 call sites in Sirene state handlers before the shared pose renderer invokes Boss_UpdateSirenePoseScript. They are dc.w command streams ending in $FFFF, $FFFF, and $FFFE respectively. This establishes the direct interpreter path, not a visual pose identity. The three state-14 scripts are excluded because the state stores their pointers through two lookup tables, and the frame-data base at $057D18 is not a command stream.

reviews.basis: Boss_EnterSireneState14 selects this word command record through one of two four-pointer tables and stores it in $71C(a5); Boss_RenderSireneState14 later loads the pointer into a1 for the pose interpreter.
reviews.reason: Sirene_State14PoseScriptSet0 has entries 0/0/2/2 and Set1 has 0/0/1/1. Boss_EnterSireneState14 selects a set from field $54, masks RandomNumberState by $C for longword offsets 0, 4, 8, or 12, and writes the selected pointer to $71C(a5). Boss_RenderSireneState14 later loads it into a1 before Boss_RenderSirenePose. Each script has a first $FFFE stop marker. Script2 contains four additional command words and a second $FFFE after its first stop; no direct symbolic pointer to that tail is known, so reachability of those words is not claimed.

reviews.basis: The DAC descriptor tables encode this 0x8000-byte ROM-aligned PCM bank through its high address byte plus per-sample offsets.
reviews.reason: PCMPart1 through PCMPart8 occupy eight consecutive $8000-byte asset ranges from $098000 to $0D8000, and pcm_samples.s includes each under the matching Sound_PCMBank1..8 label. Sound_PCMSampleDescriptors and Sound_VoiceDACDescriptors encode these bank bases with (Sound_PCMBankN >> $8) followed by per-sample offset/length words. PCMPart9 begins at $0D8000 but has only $1A5E bytes before padding, so its unique evidence correctly excludes it from this uniform-size group. The bank names and format are structural evidence, not identification of individual voice samples.

reviews.basis: Periodic-shot enemy animation streams reference this address-ordered composite sprite mapping.
reviews.reason: PeriodicShotEnemySpriteAnimationPointers selects Wait, Transition, or Attack streams. Their relative frame references cover all seven mappings: Wait visits 03/00/01/02/04/02/01/00/03, Attack visits 00/05/06/05, and Transition visits 00/05/03. Each of the seven mapping records has nine six-byte sprite entries, with the high bit set on the final entry. The ROM-order suffix does not assert a visual pose or runtime visit to every stream.

reviews.basis: At least one of Midgame_LightningSpriteAnimation00/01/03 selects this ROM-ordered sprite-mapping record through a relative frame offset; neither a visual pose nor multiple sprite pieces is implied.
reviews.reason: Midgame_UpdateRandomLightningEffect masks RandomNumberState with $C and selects one of four animation pointers. Streams 00, 01, and 03 select exactly this seven-record family through relative dc.w frame offsets; stream 02 instead uses records 07-12. Mapping00-06 contain 4/5/4/3/3/2/1 six-byte sprite entries respectively, so the old shared 'composite' claim was false for mapping06. Each record terminates through the high bit on its final sprite entry. The ROM-order suffix does not assert a visual pose.

reviews.basis: Joker's descriptors reference this directional mapping-pointer table.
reviews.reason: Boss_JokerMetaspriteDescriptors references all six 0x20-byte tables, directly or with attribute bits in the high address portion. Each contains eight longword sprite-mapping pointers. A/B are forward/reverse A0-A7, C/D are forward/reverse C0-C7, and E/F are forward/reverse E0-E7. This proves the static pointer-table structure and ordered rotation frames, not the visible direction of a particular index.

reviews.basis: Shellshogun's descriptors reference this directional mapping-pointer table.
reviews.reason: Boss_ShellshogunMetaspriteDescriptors references all six 0x20-byte tables with packed high-word attributes. Each contains eight longword sprite-mapping pointers: A/B/C descend 26-19, 10-03, and 18-11, while D/E/F ascend 19-26, 03-10, and 11-18. Boss_ShellshogunUpdateSpriteFlip also indexes F directly with an angle-derived offset masked to $1C. The shared basis asserts only descriptor ownership and pointer-table format; no visual orientation is assigned to a particular index.

reviews.basis: Boss_ZLeoValkirieForceSharedMetaspriteData embeds this exact mapping pointer in its part descriptors; the table is statically shared by both initializers.
reviews.reason: The 16-longword descriptor run at $0355A4 contains three zero entries, one Z-Leo blade mapping, and pointers to all five reviewed mappings: A/B/C three times each, D twice, E once. Boss_ZLeoIntroInit passes that run as a0 to Sprite_InitializeLinkedMetaspriteParts with separate radii and links at a1/a2. Boss_ValkirieForceInit passes the same base as a0/a1/a2, so its non-descriptor inputs reinterpret these bytes; static shared address does not prove identical runtime use of each mapping. The five records contain 4/2/1/1/2 six-byte sprite pieces in A/B/C/D/E order, each high-bit-terminated. The suffixes distinguish descriptor targets, not visual identity or ROM order.

reviews.basis: Enemy behavior animation streams reference this address-ordered composite sprite mapping.
reviews.reason: Both Enemy_BehaviorWaitSpriteAnimation and Enemy_BehaviorGroundedSpriteAnimation reference mappings 00-04 in order; the wait stream then reverses through 03-01, and the grounded stream repeats 04 before reversing to 00. The attack-cooldown stream also references mapping 00. The five records contain 5/4/4/6/6 six-byte sprite pieces in ROM order; only the final piece in each carries the terminator bit. These references establish stream membership and composite format, not a visual pose identity.

reviews.basis: Enemy_CirclingLoopAnimation stores a self-relative pointer to this high-bit-terminated sprite mapping.
reviews.reason: Enemy_CirclingAnimationMappings points to Enemy_CirclingLoopAnimation. That stream names mappings A-E in order with duration 2 after each and ends with a self-relative loop pointer and zero control word. All five mapping records consist of one six-byte piece with its terminator bit set. The adjacent rotation mappings belong to another selector, and A-E asserts sequence membership rather than visible facing.

reviews.basis: Player_WeaponAnimationFrames selects this sprite mapping at the stated weapon-animation index.
reviews.reason: Player_SetWeaponAnimationData uses the frame offset in d1 to read Player_WeaponAnimationFrames. The six longword slots name mappings 00-04 in index order, followed by the distinct Player_DashSecondarySpriteMapping; the reviewed set covers only the five Player_WeaponAnimationSpriteMapping records. Player_UpdateWeaponAnim advances its offset by four and wraps at $18. The suffixes are table indices, not the order of every player pose in ROM or a visual weapon identity.

reviews.basis: Player_PrimaryAnimationLayoutTable contains this sprite mapping at the stated index and Player_PrepareSpriteRendering selects it through the terrain animation-index tables.
reviews.reason: Player_PrepareSpriteRendering installs Player_PrimaryAnimationLayoutTable and Player_PrepareSpriteRendering_WithTables selects a longword through either terrain animation-index table; their entries are multiples of four from 0 through $10. The table lists mappings 00-04 in index order, then separate offset bytes. The mapping records occur in ROM order 04/03/00/02/01, so suffixes state table index rather than physical order or visual pose.

reviews.basis: Player_AlternateAnimationLayoutTable contains this sprite mapping at the stated index and the alternate rendering path selects it through the terrain animation-index tables.
reviews.reason: Alternate player rendering paths pass Player_AlternateAnimationLayoutTable in a0 to Player_PrepareSpriteRendering_WithTables, which uses the same lower/upper terrain index tables as the primary path. Its five longword slots list mappings 00-04 in index order, followed by separate offset bytes. The mapping records instead occur in ROM order 04/03/00/02/01; suffixes state table index, not physical order or a visible pose.

reviews.basis: The routine loads its adjacent descriptor into a0 and tail-calls Tilemap_QueueIndexedColumns.
reviews.reason: The three $053A3A/$053A52/$053A6A wrappers each load the matching adjacent MissirayTileTransferSet00/01/02Descriptor into a0, execute nop, then tail-jump to Tilemap_QueueIndexedColumns. Set 03 instead belongs to a wait-state routine and is not a member. The suffixes identify matching descriptor slots, not a guessed visual tile effect.

reviews.basis: The adjacent Missiray loader passes this word record in a0 to Tilemap_QueueIndexedColumns.
reviews.reason: Wrappers 00-02 and the set-03 wait state each load their matching descriptor address into a0 before tail-jumping to Tilemap_QueueIndexedColumns. Sets 00-02 have six words headed by $6020/$2000/$0102; set 03 has five words headed by $6020/$2000/$0101. Tilemap_QueueIndexedColumns reads bytes 4 and 5 as loop counts, so a uniform six-word claim would be false. Set 03 has no separate named loader.

reviews.basis: The routine passes its adjacent indexed-row descriptor directly to Tilemap_QueueIndexedRows.
reviews.reason: Each reviewed wrapper loads its adjacent indexed-row descriptor into a0, executes nop, and tail-jumps to Tilemap_QueueIndexedRows: sets 00, 02, 03, 04 and 05. Set 01 instead falls through to a shared jump tail; set 06 is embedded in the rise-state threshold path. Their exclusion is deliberate. The five descriptor bodies are seven words each, but carry different destination/index words and are not assumed to show the same tiles.

reviews.basis: Direct references from the options/frontend renderer establish the table's consumer and displayed role.
reviews.reason: UI_UpdateMessageOption, UI_UpdateBGMOption and UI_UpdateSFXOption pass On as a1 and Off as a2; UI_UpdateDifficultyOption passes SuperEasy as a1 and SuperHard as a2. Options_ApplyToggleAndQueueLabels copies each choice only until its first $FFFF word. The exact first-string lengths are 4/3/10/9 tile words in On/Off/SuperEasy/SuperHard order. Two additional terminated strings follow SuperHard in ROM but are outside this direct reader's first string; no visual or reachability claim is made for them.

reviews.basis: The type-$410 Stage 24 object's relative-offset animation selects this sprite mapping record; the frame suffix preserves ROM order.
reviews.reason: StageTransition_InitializeStage24SceneObjects assigns type $410 to Entity57; slot $410/4 of Entity_UpdateHandlerTable dispatches its Stage24SceneObject states, and HoldExpandedFrame installs Stage24SceneObject_SpriteAnimation in field 8. The animation lists the five reviewed mapping labels as consecutive Frame01-Frame05 relative offsets after Frame00, with timing words 8/8/9/8/8; Anim_ResolveTimedMappingFrame resolves such offsets for Sprite_RenderObjectList. The suffix follows ROM and stream order, not an inferred appearance.

reviews.basis: Antroid's secondary descriptor array references this three-word inline sprite descriptor.
reviews.reason: The secondary Antroid metasprite descriptor array includes D/F/E/G at slots 0/2/7/9, each with the +1 inline-descriptor marker. At $03499E/$0349A4/$0349AA/$0349B0, each target contains exactly three dc.w fields before the next label. Boss_AntroidInitializeBattleState passes this array to Sprite_InitializeAdditionalLinkedMetaspriteParts, whose low-bit branch handles inline descriptors. The letters encode ROM order, not visual identity.

reviews.basis: Back Stringer's descriptors reference this directional mapping-pointer table.
reviews.reason: Back Stringer's linked-part initializer receives Boss_BackStringerMetaspriteDescriptors. That descriptor list references each A-D rotation table, with repeated C/A/D/B slots and attribute flags; the common metasprite initializer follows its rotation-frame branch. Each table holds eight dc.l mapping pointers. A/B traverse set A in opposite orders, and C/D traverse set C in opposite orders. No on-screen direction is assigned to any suffix.

reviews.basis: Madam Barbar's descriptors reference this directional mapping-pointer table.
reviews.reason: Madam Barbar's setup passes Boss_MadamBarbarMetaspriteDescriptors to Sprite_InitializeLinkedMetaspriteParts. That descriptor list references each A-D rotation table, sometimes with high-bit attribute flags; the initializer's rotation-frame branch handles them. Each table holds eight dc.l mapping pointers. B reverses A's set-A order, while C/D traverse set B in ascending/descending order. No on-screen direction is assigned to any suffix.

reviews.basis: The frames before that timer expires return here.
reviews.reason: All four Phase Pattern states start by decrementing $48(a5) and use bne.s to reach their own return label while the countdown is nonzero. At zero, each performs its distinct state/animation/motion update and falls through to the same RTS: WaitBeforeAttack selects $14 and state +2; BeginHorizontalMotion selects $1C and sets $18 to -1; StopHorizontalMotion clears $18 and selects $18; Restart restores the $100 wait, animation 4, and state 2. The shared sentence covers only the nonzero-countdown branch, not identical expiry effects.

reviews.basis: The three shared projectile streams reference this high-bit-terminated sprite mapping and differ only in their per-frame durations.
reviews.reason: SharedProjectileDuration2/4/8Animation each lists mappings A-D in the same order, with timing words 2/4/8 respectively for the first three frames and $FF after the fourth. Each mapping is one three-word sprite command whose first word has bit 15 set. Boss_SnakeShotMappingChoices references all three streams; duration 4 also has direct installs in Stage 12, Gusthead, shared directional volley, and bouncing-object code. The older blanket Stage 18 direct-consumer claim has no matching symbolic install in the current source and is not retained. Letters encode ROM order, not visible poses.

reviews.basis: Xi-Tiger's descriptors reference this directional mapping-pointer table.
reviews.reason: Boss_XiTigerSetup passes Boss_XiTigerMetaspriteDescriptors to Sprite_InitializeLinkedMetaspriteParts, whose rotation-frame branch stores the table pointer. That descriptor list references all four A-D tables, sometimes with high-bit attributes. Each table holds eight longword mapping pointers: A and C traverse Xi-Tiger rotation set A in ascending and descending order, while B and D do the same for set B. The suffixes record ROM order, not a visual direction.

reviews.basis: The wrapper supplies D7 value eighteen and the shared interpolation workspace to Anim_InitializePoseChannelsFromBytes.
reviews.reason: Each of the four reviewed wrappers executes moveq #$12,d7, points a1 at SharedPatternRow0Long0, and tail-jumps to Anim_InitializePoseChannelsFromBytes with source bytes in a0. The shared routine writes one shifted word and one zero-delta word per source byte, then dbf d7 repeats: an initial $12 means nineteen channels. One original Valkirie viewer wrapper instead passes $10 and is deliberately not included.

reviews.basis: A stage-specific initializer or graphics path selects this exact 30-byte record address before Stage_ApplyConfigurationRecord consumes its fixed fields and palette-list pointer.
reviews.reason: Stage_InitializerOffsets selects Stage_ApplyStage1Configuration, Stage_ApplyStage2Configuration, and Stage_InitializeStage8 at StageTableIndex offsets $00, $02, and $0E. Each wrapper loads its corresponding record into A0 and reaches Stage_ApplyConfigurationRecord, which consumes 30 bytes in the declared field order and passes the final palette-list pointer to Gfx_LoadMultiplePalettes. These are three exact records, not evidence that every stage initializer has identical side effects: Stage 8 also initializes tilemap ranges.

reviews.basis: Only the adjacent unreferenced Stage 20 variant wrapper selects this 30-byte record.
reviews.reason: The four consecutive 30-byte records start with distinct StageStateOffset values $28/$30/$38/$40 and share the same palette offset list. Each is loaded by the adjacent matching variant wrapper, then passed to Stage_ApplyConfigurationRecord; the wrappers also fill four tilemap word ranges. None of these wrappers appears in Stage_InitializerOffsets, whose Stage 20 slot selects Stage_InitializeStage20 and its separate Stage20ConfigRecord. 'Unreferenced' is limited to the current source-level static call/dispatch graph, not a proof of runtime unreachability via indirect pointers.

reviews.basis: Control words $FFFE and $FFFF select termination or looping.
reviews.reason: All three Valkirie debug-viewer interpreters load a word from their pose script, store $FFFE into offset $58 and return, or clear offsets $58 and $29C on $FFFF before reading from the script start. The primary script contains both words; the shorter secondary and tertiary scripts contain $FFFF. This reviews the shared interpreter behavior, not a claim that both commands occur in every script.

reviews.basis: Orphaned_EnemySpawnClearDirectorData writes zero to this longword; no other reconstructed source reads or writes it, so its purpose beyond that store is unknown.
reviews.reason: The no-static-caller routine at $02C3A8 zeroes D0, then writes the delay timer and the three consecutive longwords at $FFFF811A, $FFFF811E, and $FFFF8122. The source contains no other uses of those three RAM names. The A/B/C suffixes indicate address order only; no downstream game behavior is inferred.

reviews.basis: Enemy_BehaviorMovementSpriteAnimation references this address-ordered composite sprite mapping.
reviews.reason: Enemy_UpdateBehaviorAnimation indexes the behavior pointer table from state word $5C(a5); its movement entry selects Enemy_BehaviorMovementSpriteAnimation. That stream references mapping 05, then exact mappings 06, 07, and 08 in order, each for four ticks, before a zero-duration relative jump to its start. The 06–08 suffixes record ROM order, not independently observed appearance.

reviews.basis: Enemy_BehaviorAttackCooldownSpriteAnimation references this address-ordered composite sprite mapping.
reviews.reason: Enemy_MainStateMachine_BeginAttackCooldown writes $10 to state word $5C(a5), selecting the fourth behavior pointer-table entry. Its stream uses mappings 00/09/10/11/10/09 with timer words 3/6/8/$10/8/$FF. The final $FF is a hold marker: Anim_ResolveTimedMappingFrame tests its low byte as negative and skips sequence advancement until another state selects a stream. No visual pose is inferred from the three reviewed mapping addresses.

reviews.basis: Enemy_BehaviorDefeatSpriteAnimation references this address-ordered composite sprite mapping.
reviews.reason: Enemy_ConvertToDefeatProjectile directly installs this stream in object field 8. It references mappings 12/14/13/14 with durations 3/2/3/2, then a zero-duration relative jump back to the stream start. The repeated 14 reference is deliberate; the neutral mapping suffixes record ROM order without a visual-identity claim.

reviews.basis: Stage18_SegmentedWormDirectionFramesA references this address-ordered worm mapping.
reviews.reason: The first pointer in Stage18_SegmentedWormDirectionFrameTables selects A. Its sixteen entries use indices 00/03/02/01 twice, then 00/01/02/03 twice; exact mappings 01, 02, and 03 each occur four times. The suffixes describe ROM order, not a guessed cardinal direction or pose.

reviews.basis: Stage18_SegmentedWormDirectionFramesB references this address-ordered worm mapping.
reviews.reason: The second pointer in Stage18_SegmentedWormDirectionFrameTables selects B. Its sixteen entries use indices 04/07/06/05 twice, then 04/05/06/07 twice; exact mappings 05, 06, and 07 each occur four times. No visual direction is inferred from the table position.

reviews.basis: Stage18_SegmentedWormDirectionFramesC references this address-ordered worm mapping.
reviews.reason: The third pointer in Stage18_SegmentedWormDirectionFrameTables selects C. Its sixteen entries use indices 08/11/10/09 twice, then 08/09/10/11 twice; exact mappings 09, 10, and 11 each occur four times. The reviewed claim is table membership, not an unobserved sprite pose.

reviews.basis: LoadFuncToRAM reads this $200 source word as a byte count and copies 512 bytes starting at the following ROM byte to RAM $FFFFEE00; RTE does not terminate the fixed copy.
reviews.reason: Each of the three install lists has operation 0, a pointer to its own $200 source word, destination $EE00, and $FFFF terminator. LoadObjData operation 0 selects LoadFuncToRAM, which shifts the source word right by two and executes 128 longword copies. The source ranges start at $0019D8, $001B7A, and $001C78; the first two 512-byte ranges extend across the next install list. These are exact fixed-copy fields, not disassembled handler extents.

reviews.basis: Low-bit-tagged metasprite entries point here; Sprite_InitializeLinkedMetaspriteParts reads its three words into child fields $E, $8, and $A.
reviews.reason: The shared Seven Forces descriptor tables reference each of the three exact six-byte records as label+1. Sprite_InitializeLinkedMetaspriteParts clears pointer bit zero before the inline path, then reads three words into child $E, $8, and $A. The records contain distinct word triples $042D/$0F00/$F0F0, $043D/$0A00/$F4F4, and $0446/$0500/$F8F8; no visual pose or unsupported meaning for child $8/$A is inferred.

reviews.basis: Boss_MadamBarbarMetaspriteDescriptors references this three-word record with a low-bit tag; Sprite_InitializeLinkedMetaspriteParts copies its words into child fields $E, $8, and $A.
reviews.reason: Boss_MadamBarbarSetupState passes Boss_MadamBarbarMetaspriteDescriptors to Sprite_InitializeLinkedMetaspriteParts. Its table contains label+1 pointers to each of the three exact six-byte records; the shared inline path removes that low bit and copies the words to child $E/$8/$A. A/B/C contain $6390/$0F00/$F0F0, $63A0/$0A00/$F4F4, and $43C4/$0000/$FCFC respectively. The letters are neutral ROM-order identifiers.

reviews.basis: Antroid's primary descriptor array references this three-word inline sprite descriptor.
reviews.reason: Boss_AntroidInitializeBattleState passes Boss_AntroidPrimaryMetaspriteDescriptors to the linked-part initializer. The primary array contains low-bit-tagged pointers to both reviewed six-byte records B and C, as well as A. B has words $0325/$0A00/$F4F4; C has $0315/$0F00/$F0F0. The shared inline path copies these words into child $E/$8/$A; the suffixes do not claim visual identity.

reviews.basis: Shellshogun's descriptor array references this three-word inline sprite descriptor.
reviews.reason: Boss_ShellshogunSetupPhase passes Boss_ShellshogunMetaspriteDescriptors to the linked-part initializer. Its low-bit-tagged entries reference six-byte A ($6457/$0A00/$F4F4) and B ($6460/$0500/$F8F8), both more than once. Their words are copied into child $E/$8/$A, not decoded here as named visual poses.

reviews.basis: Xi-Tiger's descriptor array references this three-word inline sprite descriptor.
reviews.reason: Boss_XiTigerSetup passes Boss_XiTigerMetaspriteDescriptors to the linked-part initializer. Tagged entries reference exact records A ($62D4/$0500/$F8F8), B ($62D8/$0A00/$F4F4), and C ($62E1/$0A00/$F4F4); some entries also carry high-bit flags while retaining pointer bit zero. The shared inline path strips bit zero and copies three words to child $E/$8/$A.

reviews.basis: Joker's descriptor array references this three-word inline sprite descriptor.
reviews.reason: Boss_JokerSetup supplies Boss_JokerMetaspriteDescriptors to the linked-part initializer. Low-bit-tagged entries select A ($636E/$0500/$F8F8) and B ($6366/$0500/$F8F8), including entries with additional high-bit flags. The shared inline path copies the exact three words to child $E/$8/$A; letters denote address order.

reviews.basis: Sharpssteel's descriptor array references this three-word inline sprite descriptor.
reviews.reason: Boss_SharpssteelInitializeState supplies Boss_SharpssteelMetaspriteDescriptors to the linked-part initializer. Its tagged entries select A ($63F9/$0A00/$F4F4) and B ($6402/$0500/$F8F8), each at exact six-byte record boundaries. The shared inline path copies these three words into child $E/$8/$A without proving an additional visual label.

reviews.basis: Wolf Garopa's descriptors reference this directional mapping-pointer table.
reviews.reason: Boss_WolfGaropaInitialize passes Boss_WolfGaropaMetaspriteDescriptors to Sprite_InitializeLinkedMetaspriteParts. That descriptor array references each exact 32-byte A/B/C table with $18000000 high-bit flags. Each table consists of eight mapping pointers consumed through the initializer's rotation-frame branch; A/B/C are ROM-order labels, not independently verified visual poses.

reviews.basis: Valkirie's primary descriptor array references this directional mapping-pointer table.
reviews.reason: Debug_ValkirieViewerInitialize passes Boss_ValkirieMetaspriteDescriptors to Sprite_InitializeLinkedMetaspriteParts. The array references exact 32-byte A/B/C eight-pointer tables: A and B with $18000000 high-bit flags, C without those flags. The initializer's bit-22 test still routes all three even-pointer forms through its rotation-frame branch; C reuses mapping pointers within its eight slots. The table letters denote ROM order, not independently verified visual poses.

reviews.basis: Stage and weapon-setup paths fill this complete 64-word row.
reviews.reason: PlaneTilemapRow26/27/28 are consecutive $80-byte work-RAM rows. WeaponSetup_InitializeColorTables writes all three with move.w through a DBF loop seeded at $3F, and Stage_PrepareFourWordRangesWithD writes the same three plus row 25 with the same 64-iteration bound. These row names describe shared buffer position, not exclusive ownership by either path.

reviews.basis: Midgame_LightningSpriteAnimation02 references this address-ordered composite sprite mapping.
reviews.reason: Midgame_LightningSpriteAnimation02 contains relative-offset entries for each exact mapping 08/09/10 in sequence, each followed by duration three. The three records occupy distinct ROM ranges and terminate their composite mapping at a high-bit word; neither their visual appearance nor a unique runtime owner is inferred from the table alone.

reviews.basis: Stage12_TeddyBearRescueAnimation and SharedTeddyHazardLoopAnimation reference this mapping.
reviews.reason: Both relative-offset animation streams select the exact A/B/C composite mapping records. Each record holds four three-word pieces ending with a high-bit word. Both streams use A/B/C/B order, but rescue has durations 5/4/5/4 while the shared loop has 2/1/2/1; common mapping membership does not make the animations identical.

reviews.basis: The shared loop is installed by the Teddy Bear initializer and by both Stage 15 hazard-wave initializers.
reviews.reason: Stage12_TeddyBearInit assigns SharedTeddyHazardLoopAnimation to object field 8, as do both Stage 15 hazard-wave initialization paths. That stream reaches exact A/B/C mapping records through relative offsets; the separate Teddy Bear rescue stream also reaches them but is not claimed to be installed by the Stage 15 paths.

reviews.basis: This terminated LoadObjData descriptor loads the shared transition asset at VRAM $E000.
reviews.reason: Each of the three state-two graphics loaders passes its adjacent descriptor to LoadObjData. Each exact descriptor is type 7, points to CreditsAndTransitionTileArtE000, supplies destination $E000, and ends with $FFFF. The shared source and destination are proven; the three enclosing transition state machines remain distinct.

reviews.basis: A 0xFF marker flushes the final DMA length and publishes the updated command-queue head and staging-data cursor.
reviews.reason: Both byte-stream parsers branch to their own FinishStream label for marker $FF. The exact terminal instruction blocks are identical: write d1 to -(a1), store a1 as VDPCommandQueueHead, store a2 as VDPStagingDataCursor, and return. Their earlier record parsing differs (headered versus headerless), but that distinction does not change this terminal action.

reviews.basis: State two only publishes byte FFA958 when global wait FF80C2 clears.
reviews.reason: Both type-$3F0 and type-$3F4 state tables select their own UpdateWaitFlag label for state two. Each label tests MessageSequenceState and writes one to SceneSequenceFlags only when that word is zero; their separate return labels preserve the two exact addresses.

reviews.basis: This unreferenced entry reads controller up/down, adjusts angle, advances a fixed pose, and renders composite parts.
reviews.reason: Both viewer Update entries test ControllerHeldState bits two and three, adjust $56(a5) by two, mask the angle with $1FE, select their own fixed PoseScript, call their own pose interpreter, and tail-jump to Sprite_BeginMetaspritePartTraversal. No reconstructed static caller reaches either entry; this review does not assert runtime reachability.

reviews.basis: The interpreter reads event, control, or timed target commands.
reviews.reason: Each ReadNextPoseCommand path reads script offset $58(a5), handles event prefix $80, passes word $FFFE to a stop path, passes $FFFF to a loop-reset path, and otherwise selects a timed target command. The two local scripts and target bases remain separate.

reviews.basis: The active path decrements timer $C(a5), sets d7=$12, and calls Anim_AdvancePoseChannelInterpolation; its inclusive DBF loop advances nineteen channels.
reviews.reason: Both exact tick labels execute subq.w #1,$C(a5), select SharedPatternRow0Long0, set d7=$12, and call Anim_AdvancePoseChannelInterpolation. That callee's DBF iterates nineteen times, correcting the former eighteen-value statement.

reviews.basis: The path calls its pose interpreter, sets d7=$19 as count-minus-one, and tail-jumps to Sprite_BeginMetaspritePartTraversal; the shared helper converts that to a count of 26.
reviews.reason: Both AdvancePoseAndRender paths call their corresponding pose interpreter, load d7=$19, and jump to Sprite_BeginMetaspritePartTraversal. Sprite_SetMetaspriteTraversalPointers stores d7 as MetaspritePartCountM1 and Sprite_LoadMetaspritePartCount adds one, so the resulting count is 26, not the old claimed 25. This states the requested traversal count, not how many live parts exist.

reviews.basis: The unreferenced viewer entry passes this fixed command stream to its pose interpreter.
reviews.reason: The secondary and tertiary ViewerUpdate paths each load their own ten-byte PoseScript via LEA before branching to the local interpreter; both streams contain the same two four-byte target commands followed by $FFFF. Static source contains no call to either ViewerUpdate entry, so no visual or executed-behavior claim follows.

reviews.basis: Both readiness-wait outcomes return here.
reviews.reason: Each type-$3F0/$3F4 wait state branches to its own WaitReturn RTS while MessageSequenceState is nonzero and falls through to that same RTS after writing SceneSequenceFlags when the wait clears. The two labels are distinct ROM addresses with the same local convergence role.

reviews.basis: Command $FFFF resets script offset and command count.
reviews.reason: Both local HandlePoseLoopCommand labels compare d3 with $FFFF, clear $58(a5) and $29C(a5) on equality, and branch back to their own ReadNextPoseCommand labels. The non-$FFFF branch goes to the distinct timed-command path.

reviews.basis: Normal commands resolve a target record and initialize timed interpolation.
reviews.reason: Each BeginPoseCommandInterpolation label saves PoseCommandWord, masks its low byte, sign-extends the script target offset, adds its own PoseTargets base, calls its own interpolation wrapper, loads PoseDurationByte into $C(a5), and advances script offset/count. The wrappers differ in the source base loaded into a1, which is not hidden by the shared claim.

reviews.basis: The adjusted angle is wrapped and the fixed pose script is selected.
reviews.reason: Both PreparePoseUpdate labels mask angle field $56(a5) with $1FE, load their own fixed PoseScript into a1, and branch to the local AdvancePoseAndRender path. They do not imply identical pose-target source tables or runtime reachability.

reviews.basis: Pressed bit two in OptionsPressedCopy selects the previous index and sets OptionsCursorFlashTimer to six; otherwise control branches to the next-input check.
reviews.reason: The SFX and Voice CheckPrimaryInput labels have the same three-instruction gate: BTST bit two of OptionsPressedCopy, BEQ to their own CheckNext label, and store six in OptionsCursorFlashTimer before the prior-index branch. Their later selection bodies differ: SFX queues navigation sound and wraps at $98, while Voice wraps at $25 without that sound call.

reviews.basis: Pressed bit three in OptionsPressedCopy enters next-index selection and sets OptionsCursorFlashTimer to six; otherwise the current index is stored and rendered.
reviews.reason: The SFX and Voice CheckNextInput labels each BTST bit three of OptionsPressedCopy, branch to their own StoreAndRender label when clear, and store six in OptionsCursorFlashTimer when pressed. Only this input gate is shared: SFX queues navigation sound and wraps at $98; Voice wraps at $25 without that sound call.

reviews.basis: Many mutually exclusive scene and boss users overlap this range, so the physical row name does not claim one subsystem owner.
reviews.reason: Effect_ApplyTransitionMask names the two consecutive 32-byte rows separately, initializes a0 and a1 to their bases, and processes two post-increment longwords from each per DBF iteration for four iterations. Z-Leo and other encounter paths reuse the same physical workspace, so neither SharedPatternRow base claims exclusive ownership. The common sentence applies only to the two physical row bases, whose distinct exact ranges are stated in their other basis entries.

reviews.basis: After initialization, execution enters here to test the segment's health and dispatch defeat to the shared explosion handler.
reviews.reason: Both Caterpillar entity handlers skip initialization once state word 4(a5) is set, then enter their own Update label. Each tests $24(a5), branches on nonnegative value to its own Position label, and otherwise jumps to Boss_CaterpillarSpawnExplosion. The four-phase handler initializes $24 to $58, whereas the two-phase handler initializes it to $6E; their later mapping cycles differ and are not covered by this common sentence.

reviews.basis: After selecting one of two linked parts, this branch tests its Y coordinate before applying attack impact.
reviews.reason: Antroid leap variants A and B select the FifteenthEntityType or TwentySixthEntityType pointer into a0 according to 6(a5), then at their respective CheckContact labels compare $14(a0) with $14E. Both skip impact while below the threshold and otherwise call Boss_AntroidApplyAttackImpact. The subsequent negative-result and next-preparation targets differ between variants, so the review covers only the common contact gate.

reviews.basis: All linked-record outcomes advance to the next $60-byte body record.
reviews.reason: Both Shield Viper flip walkers start with d7=$18 and a0=a5. Each Advance label is reached after either the ordinary linked-record path, the zero-link branch, or the non-$370 branch; it executes lea $60(a0),a0 and DBF back to its own loop. One walker derives the horizontal-flip bit from the frame, while the other forces bit $2000, so only the common record stride and convergence are reviewed.

reviews.basis: A zero request leaves the current animation in place.
reviews.reason: Both animation updaters load request word $5C(a5) into d0 and branch to their own RTS when zero, before either writes the animation pointer at 8(a5) or clears cursor $C(a5). Nonzero requests subtract four and index different tables: PeriodicShotEnemySpriteAnimationPointers for the enemy and Enemy_ProjectileAnimationPointers for the projectile. Only the zero-request gate is common.

reviews.basis: Both the paced frames and a full pool return here.
reviews.reason: Effect_SpawnParticleLoop and Projectile_FallingSpawner each decrement timer $48(a5) and branch to their own RTS while it remains nonnegative. After reloading that timer with two, both call Projectile_FindFreeSlotForward and branch to the same local RTS on nonzero allocation result. Their spawned object types and setup paths differ; this sentence states only the two return conditions.

reviews.basis: An active initial timer, clear terrain test, or failed impact allocation returns through this RTS.
reviews.reason: Both type-$148 and type-$254 two-speed collision handlers decrement $48(a5) during phase zero and branch to their own RTS while it is nonnegative. Their terrain path calls Collision_CheckProjectileTile and branches there on zero; their impact path calls Projectile_FindFreeSlotReverse and branches there on nonzero. The record names and source comments retain the distinct object-table types; this review covers only the three common return gates.

reviews.basis: Both completion paths continue from here into the recurring Sirene camera-shake update.
reviews.reason: Stage_SevenForcesAdvanceSireneShake and Stage_SevenForcesFinishSireneShake each contain an unconditional BRA to Stage_SevenForcesUpdateSireneShake. Both are also branch targets when SceneSequenceFlags is clear. The first transition otherwise queues sound and moves the player, whereas the second arms SevenForcesTimer; the shared claim covers only the camera-shake continuation.

reviews.basis: Both ordinary and wrapped source-pointer paths converge here before continuing the 52-byte row.
reviews.reason: The left and right completed-logo loops each initialize d5=$33, so DBF admits 52 source-byte iterations per row. Each ContinueSource label executes DBF d5 to its own NextSourceByte label. The left loop decrements a0 and wraps it by -$78; the right increments a0 and wraps it by +$78, so the shared sentence covers only the convergence and row count.

reviews.basis: Both pose-cursor anchor choices converge here to copy the selected linked-object pointer into fields $48/$4A before updating parts.
reviews.reason: Both Madam Barbar Anchor labels set the chosen linked object's Y word $14(a0) to $C8, copy a0 into $48(a5) and $4A(a5), then branch to Boss_MadamBarbarUpdateParts. The left-side selector chooses between entities 26/27 at pose offsets 8/$C, while the right-side selector chooses 28/29 at 4/$10. The shared claim does not merge those candidate lists.

reviews.basis: Both prefixed and ordinary commands converge here to read the control word and test stop marker $FFFE.
reviews.reason: Madam Barbar and Joker each branch around an optional $80 sound-command prefix to a ReadPoseControlWord label, or consume that prefix and fall through to the same label. Each label reads (a1,d0.w) into d3, compares it with $FFFE, stores the stop word in $58(a5), and returns when equal. Their later loop-command and interpolation paths remain separate.

reviews.basis: Both slot-selection paths converge here to bind the active part, align its Y coordinate, and render the metasprite.
reviews.reason: Terobuster missile attacks A and B each choose between SixthEntityType and EleventhEntityType according to $A(a5) and pose-cursor thresholds. Their BindPart labels perform the same four instructions: store a0 in $48(a5) and $4A(a5), set Y $14(a0) to $14C, and branch to Boss_TerobusterUpdateMetaspriteAndProjectile. A tests pose range 5..$17 and B tests $10..$1F; the review covers only the common bind and dispatch.

reviews.basis: Descriptor byte five is copied here and selection compares its upper priority bits with new requests.
reviews.reason: Sound_WritePrimaryVoiceDACMailbox copies 5(a0) to Z80VoiceSlotAFlags, while Sound_WriteSecondaryVoiceDACMailbox copies it to Z80VoiceSlotBFlags. Sound_SelectVoiceDACPlaybackSlot reads both flags, masks their upper bits with $C0, and compares the selected slot priority with the incoming descriptor. The two mailbox addresses are $20 bytes apart and retain separate A/B ownership.

reviews.basis: Disabled-spawn and allocation-failure paths return here.
reviews.reason: Both Viblack emitters test frame-counter bit zero and return from their own RTS when the paced frame is skipped; both also return on nonzero result from their free-slot finder. The nearby defeat-particle path uses Projectile_FindFreeSlotForward and initializes type $88, while the transition-debris path uses Projectile_FindFreeSlotReverse and may initialize debris or type $88. Only the two early-return conditions are common.

reviews.basis: Enemy_FormationWaveSpriteAnimation references this address-ordered formation-member mapping.
reviews.reason: The animation's second and third relative frame words select Mapping01 and Mapping02, each for three ticks. Their first tile words differ ($680C and $6814), so the shared claim covers only the stream membership, not identical artwork or appearance.

reviews.basis: IndexedObjectSpriteAnimation00 and 01 reference this address-ordered sprite-mapping record; the specific object identity is not proven.
reviews.reason: Both streams reference Mapping00 in frame positions two and four and Mapping01 in position three. Their first tile words differ ($8800 and $8804), and the streams use six-tick and $13-tick durations respectively. The shared claim is limited to membership and ROM order; no specific object identity follows.

reviews.basis: IndexedObjectSpriteAnimation02 references this address-ordered sprite-mapping variant; the specific object identity is not proven.
reviews.reason: Animation02 places Mapping07 in frame positions three and seven and Mapping08 in positions five and nine, with five-tick durations. The mapping records differ in their last word ($F4F9 versus $F4F7). The shared claim covers the stream relationship only, not visual or object identity.

reviews.basis: Projectile_MissirayFallingShotSpriteAnimation references this address-ordered vertical-shot mapping.
reviews.reason: The falling-shot stream references Mapping01 in its second frame and Mapping02 in its third frame, with one-tick durations. The two records have different Y words ($E3F8/$FCF8 and $E1F8/$FEF8). Only their animation membership is shared; the visual pose is not inferred.

reviews.basis: The full-screen fade engine adds the signed step to the progress word, uses the progress high byte as the RGB delta, and stops at zero or 0x1000.
reviews.reason: PaletteFadeStep at $FFFFF75C is the signed increment and zero disables the fade. PaletteFadeProgress at $FFFFF75E is the accumulator: Palette_UpdateFullScreenFade adds the step to it, reads its high byte from the big-endian address for channel adjustment, and clamps it to zero or $1000 at the two endpoints. The shared sentence describes the relationship, not interchangeable RAM roles.

reviews.basis: Neither direction held leaves the facing unchanged.
reviews.reason: Player_UpdateAimDirection tests ControllerHeldState bits 2 and 3, sets bit 4 in $E(a5), and reaches its return without altering facing bit 3 when neither is held. Player_UpdateHorizontalFacing instead tests $69(a5) bits 2 and 3 and likewise reaches its own RTS with bit 3 of $E(a5) unchanged. The shared claim is about facing bit 3 only, not every flag or the input source.

reviews.basis: Multiple Seven Forces form descriptors reference this eight-entry frame-pointer table for directional part rendering.
reviews.reason: Table3 contains Frame16 through Frame23 in ascending order, while Table5 contains Frame24 through Frame31. Both are eight-longword runs referenced by the descriptor data below them, with Table3 also used by the auxiliary and Medusa descriptors. The claim is about pointer-table shape and consumers, not a visual pose.

reviews.basis: Multiple Seven Forces form descriptors reference this reverse-ordered frame-pointer table for directional part rendering.
reviews.reason: Table4 runs Frame23 down through Frame16, whereas Table6 runs Frame31 down through Frame24. Each is eight longwords, and both labels occur in later Seven Forces part-descriptor data. The frame ranges remain distinct; no appearance is inferred.

reviews.basis: Seven Forces form descriptors reference this reverse-ordered frame-pointer table for directional part rendering.
reviews.reason: Table2 runs Frame15 through Frame08 and is referenced by Valkirie and later form descriptors; Table8 runs Frame39 through Frame32 and is referenced by the primary Valkirie descriptor. Both are eight-entry reverse runs, but only Table2 has multiple descriptor occurrences, so the shared sentence is limited to descriptor membership and ordering.

reviews.basis: The helper disables the pair stored at offsets $48/$4A, stores d0/d1 as the new pair, and enables both selected part objects.
reviews.reason: Entity_SelectValkirieActivePartPair is the body that clears bit zero for pointers in $48/$4A(a5), stores d0/d1 into those fields, and sets bit zero on the new pointers. Entity_SelectValkirieActivePartPairAtY140 calls that body and then writes $140 to the second selected part's Y word. The common claim covers the shared call effect, not the wrapper's additional Y placement.

reviews.basis: The loop clears 128 groups of four longwords beginning at HScrollBuffer, exactly the 2,048-byte horizontal-scroll workspace.
reviews.reason: Gfx_ClearHScrollBuffer initializes a0 to HScrollBuffer, d0 to zero and d1 to $7F; Gfx_ClearHScrollBuffer_Loop is the fall-through body with four postincrement longword stores and DBF. That is 128 iterations times 16 bytes = 2048 bytes, ending at VScrollBuffer ($FFFFEC00). The entry and loop are separate addresses within one routine.

reviews.basis: The loop clears ten groups of four longwords beginning at VScrollBuffer, exactly the 160-byte vertical-scroll workspace; it does not traverse entity slots.
reviews.reason: Gfx_ClearVScrollBuffer initializes a0 to VScrollBuffer, d0 to zero and d1 to nine; its loop performs four postincrement longword stores under DBF. Ten iterations cover 160 bytes from $FFFFEC00 through $FFFFEC9F. The entry and loop are separate addresses within the same buffer-clear routine.

reviews.basis: The named Bugmax projectile initializer stores this relative-offset sprite animation in object field 8, and Anim_ResolveTimedMappingFrame consumes its frame-offset and duration pairs.
reviews.reason: Projectile_InitBugmaxSpread stores the two-frame, two-tick SpreadSpriteAnimation in 8(a0); Projectile_InitBugmaxSine stores the four-frame, six-tick SineSpriteAnimation there. Anim_ResolveTimedMappingFrame reads the relative frame word and following timer, then advances the sequence cursor. The shared claim is about the storage and consumer format, not identical projectile appearance.

reviews.basis: States that requested no animation return here.
reviews.reason: Enemy_UpdateBehaviorAnimation and Enemy_UpdateStage10WaspAnimation each load $5C(a5) and branch to their own RTS when it is zero. Nonzero state indices instead subtract four, load a different animation-pointer table into 8(a5), and clear timer $C(a5). The common claim covers only the zero-index early return; the two pointer tables remain separate.

reviews.basis: The READY/FIGHT state handlers pass this compact two-entry line descriptor to the shared message sprite-line renderer.
reviews.reason: BattleBanner_StaticSpriteLine is two longwords $C6A0010A/$680B0004, selected by HoldReadyLine and StartFightLine. BattleBanner_MovingSpriteLine is $C6AA00FF/$680B0006, selected by AnimateFightLine. Both paths feed Message_RenderLine or Message_RenderLineWithOffsets, which reach Message_WriteSpriteLine; the descriptor values and motion behavior are distinct.

reviews.basis: The active pose cursor selects which part order is installed before returning to the decision state.
reviews.reason: Missile attack A chooses d0 from 8/$18 using $A(a5), then branches to SelectPartOrderA when $58(a5)==d0 and to B otherwise. Attack B chooses $10/$20 but reverses the equality branch: non-equality selects A, equality selects B. Both exits use the pose cursor for the final A/B order choice, not the same threshold or polarity.

reviews.basis: The braking frames return here.
reviews.reason: The outward brake adds signed $4000 steps to horizontal velocity $18(a5), then returns while TST.L finds it nonzero; reaching zero selects fish Mapping02 and advances state. The inward brake uses opposite signed steps and branches directly on the post-add result, then selects Mapping01 and advances state at zero. The shared claim covers only the in-progress return.

reviews.basis: The frames before the edge return here.
reviews.reason: The inner-edge wait returns above $E0 when $E(a5) bit three is set or below $160 when it is clear, then selects Mapping00 and advances state at the edge. The outer-edge wait returns below $1A0 in its bit-three-set branch or above $A0 in its clear branch, then zeroes horizontal velocity, selects Mapping00, arms timer $40, and enters state 8. The common basis only describes the premature-edge return.

reviews.basis: The frames before the marker arrives return here.
reviews.reason: Both Z-Leo states compare PrimaryEntityXPos against $1E0 and return while the position is below that threshold. WaitMarkerPosition uses BCS and clears X velocity before advancing; WaitForMarkerEnd first increments X velocity by $1000, uses BLT, then increments a separate flag and arms timer $80 before advancing. The shared claim is limited to the below-threshold gate.

reviews.basis: Special-attack, recovery, and Seven Forces rendering paths select this secondary mapping as one of two frame-counter variants.
reviews.reason: Player_HandleSpecialAttack, Player_RenderSpecialMoveRecovery, and the Seven Forces renderers initialize a2 to MappingA, test FrameCounter low-byte bit zero, and replace a2 with MappingB when the bit is clear. MappingA begins with an A art-piece pointer; MappingB begins with a distinct B art-piece pointer. The shared claim is the selection relationship, not identical sprite artwork.

reviews.basis: State $14 chooses one of these four-entry pose-script pointer sets from the facing selector and the random phase.
reviews.reason: Boss_EnterSireneState14 initializes a0 to Set0, switches to Set1 when $54(a5) is zero, masks RandomNumberState with $C, and reads one of four longwords into $71C(a5). Set0 contains Script0/0/2/2, whereas Set1 contains Script0/0/1/1. The choice is proven by the pointers, not by visual pose identity.

reviews.basis: The corresponding graphics-set routine consumes these six pointers while configuring embedded blade parts.
reviews.reason: ConfigureBladeGraphicsSetA loads MappingsA and branches to the shared six-iteration ApplyBladeGraphicsSet loop. ConfigureBladeGraphicsSetB loads MappingsB and falls through to that same loop. Both tables contain six longword pointers, with different A/B mapping owners and different setup attribute values; the shared claim is only their consumption by the loop.

reviews.basis: The normal phase checks the derived screen coordinate against the bounded $C70..$D10 interval.
reviews.reason: Both Antroid leap branches compare $BC(a5) to $C70 and $D10 only when $1DE(a5) is zero. A exits to its finish path outside the half-open interval, while B exits to Boss_AntroidReturnToNeutralLoadAnimation; both decrement $11C(a5) inside the interval. The shared basis covers the numeric range test, not the different exit targets.

reviews.basis: The path advances the source and destination row bases before repeating the sixteen-row loop.
reviews.reason: Both title-character row continuations add four to a2, copy it to a1, and DBF d6 back to their respective row starts after d6 is initialized to $F. The left path advances source a0 by $C after reverse byte reads; the right path advances a0 by four after forward reads. The shared sentence is about row-base progression, not identical source traversal.

reviews.basis: No reconstructed call or table refers to this entrypoint.
reviews.reason: The initializer writes nine consecutive $60-byte sprite records from $360(a5), and the position updater writes those records from two anchor regions. A source-wide scan finds neither exact entrypoint name nor its ROM address in an executable call or pointer table. This is negative static evidence only; indirect runtime reachability is not asserted impossible.

reviews.basis: No reconstructed code or data reference reaches this routine.
reviews.reason: The timing helper conditionally XORs FrameTimingDebugFlag bit seven after controller tests; the other entry appends a fixed OAM record list. Neither exact routine name nor its ROM address occurs in executable source outside its definition. The OAM data's imported DATA XREF back to its owner is not a call, and no runtime reachability claim follows.

reviews.basis: No reconstructed source call or table reference reaches this helper.
reviews.reason: The first helper adjusts colors and mirrors them to a range $80 bytes away; the second wraps RGB channel additions and stores one paired color. Their exact entrypoint names and ROM addresses have no executable source reference outside the definitions. Both call or use other named palette helpers, which is outgoing use and does not establish a caller for these entries.

reviews.basis: No reconstructed static caller reaches the alternate entry.
reviews.reason: Each alternate entry is one NOP that falls into a separately named and called scroll routine. The preceding routine ends in a JMP, so it does not fall through into that NOP. No executable source instruction or pointer table names either alternate label or its ROM address; indirect entry remains unproven rather than ruled out.

reviews.basis: The adjacent unreferenced loader passes this five-record terminated graphics and mappings list to Stage_DispatchAssetListLoaderByGameMode; no reachable owner is proven.
reviews.reason: Stage 2 phase 2 and Stage 3 phase 5 each have an adjacent loader that places the list address in a0 and jumps to Stage_DispatchAssetListLoaderByGameMode. Each list contains five type/source/destination records and $FFFF, with distinct stage-specific sources and one shared final tile-art source. No static source call or pointer names either loader; the stage number is a label/provenance claim, not runtime proof of reachability.

reviews.basis: Skipped and emitted defeat-debris paths return here.
reviews.reason: The Epsilon 1 ring-object state returns here when FrameCounter modulo four is nonzero, when no free projectile slot exists, or after initializing type-$88 debris with the ring object's position. Wolf Garopa returns here on odd frames, when allocation fails, or after initializing type-$88 debris with randomized position and speed. The shared sentence describes the return role only; the two cadence and payload paths differ.

reviews.basis: The frames between shots return here.
reviews.reason: The periodic enemy shot path masks its timer with $1F and returns on nonzero phase, then also returns after an aimed-arc spawn. The Stage 11 fish state decrements $48(a5), returns while that countdown is nonzero, and after a completed volley changes state before returning; an intermediate shot instead returns directly from its burst-advance path. The shared wording refers to the wait return, not an identical shot schedule.

reviews.basis: The frames inside one step return here.
reviews.reason: Both animation helpers decrement $4C(a5) and return while the duration remains nonzero; after loading a frame they also reach the same RTS. Their negative-duration marker paths differ: UpdateScriptAndHide clears display bit 15 and returns, while UpdateLoopingScript loads a restart pointer and loops back to ReadFrame.

reviews.basis: The quotient is translated to the contiguous digit-tile range beginning at 0xB5 and appended to the staging buffer.
reviews.reason: Both emit labels add signed byte -$4B to the quotient byte, copy the result through d0 into (a2)+, then advance the divisor index and repeat. The decimal caller divides by 1/10/100/1000/10000, while the hex caller divides by 1/$10/$100/$1000; the shared emission code does not imply equal digit radices or widths.

reviews.basis: The same eight-slot forward scan.
reviews.reason: Both weapon handlers point a0 to SharedEffectObjectPool, set d7 to seven, test each slot's first word, advance a0 by $60 on occupied slots, and DBF back to the corresponding FindSlot label. The bullet and beam handlers have different cooldown and ammo setup before the scan; the common basis covers only allocation traversal.

reviews.basis: The named Stage 12 Teddy Bear state or initializer assigns this mapping/duration stream directly to the object mapping field.
reviews.reason: The collision-disabled path within Stage12_TeddyBearInit stores Stage12_TeddyBearInitialPoseAnimation in 8(a5), while Stage12_TeddyBearPilotRelease stores Stage12_TeddyBearPilotReleasePoseAnimation in the same field. Each stream has one distinct mapping-offset word followed by $FF. This proves pointer installation and stream bytes, not the rendered pose's visual identity.

reviews.basis: The pose cursor range and side field determine whether the two fixed part slots are exchanged.
reviews.reason: Both missile attack variants initialize a0/a1 from SixthEntityType and EleventhEntityType and swap them when side field $A(a5) is nonzero before the named SelectPart label. Attack A swaps again only for cursor $58 in [5,$18), while attack B does so only for [$10,$20). Both store the resulting a0 to fields $48/$4A; the different windows are not interchangeable.

reviews.basis: The set- and clear-priority paths converge on this return.
reviews.reason: Each Jampan linked-object updater compares its angle byte at $20(a5) with PrimaryEntityAngle. The unsigned-higher branch clears bit 15 of $E(a5); the other path sets that bit and branches over the clear to the same RTS. The radial updater first computes orbit X/Y, whereas the animation updater copies linked-owner X/Y; only the priority tail is shared.

reviews.basis: The state rotates, adds $4000 to vertical velocity, and disables drawing at Y $180.
reviews.reason: The two Destroyer MK2 bouncing-part handlers have the same instruction sequence: advance angle $4C by $10, mask it with $1FE for the frame selector, add $4000 to vertical velocity $1C, and store $1000 in display field 2 when Y $14 is at least $180. Separate A/B state table entries and return labels identify different object paths; no visual part identity beyond those paths is inferred.

reviews.basis: The tail prepends the VDP auto-increment and DMA-length words, then publishes both updated queue cursors.
reviews.reason: Both decimal and hex digit queue finalizers write $8F02 before $94009300 modified by d3, then publish a1 to VDPCommandQueueHead and a2 to VDPStagingDataCursor. Their preceding radix-specific conversion and divisor tables differ; the shared basis covers only the queue tail.

reviews.basis: The zero-fill entry reaches this path for every non-marker byte and appends a zero word while incrementing the DMA word count.
reviews.reason: HeaderedZeroStreamDMA and QueueZeroStreamDMA each clear d3 before entering their own byte-stream parser. Both parsers check $FE and $FF markers before testing d3, then their StageZero path clears one staging word, increments d1, and returns to ReadByte. The headered path consumes an initial word before each record; the headerless path does not.

reviews.basis: This block chooses the two terminal cursor values according to side field $0A.
reviews.reason: Missile attack A initializes d0/d1 to 8/$18 and swaps them when $A(a5) is nonzero; its subsequent equality with cursor $58 selects part order A. Missile attack B initializes $10/$20 and applies the same side-based swap, but its subsequent inequality selects part order A. The shared sentence covers terminal cursor setup, not identical exit predicates.

reviews.basis: This branch is the explicit no-play return of the adjacent frame-masked Medusa sound helper.
reviews.reason: Both Medusa sound helpers mask FrameCounter into d1 and branch to their own RTS when the masked result is nonzero, otherwise jumping to Sound_QueueSFXRequest. The first mask is three, giving a four-frame cadence; the second is seven, giving an eight-frame cadence. The return's shared role does not imply the same cadence or caller state.

reviews.basis: This descriptor field supplies the 0x40-byte copy length for the following HBlank code block.
reviews.reason: StoryDisplay and VScrollPair install lists each point to their immediately following $40 copy-length word and target RAM $EE00 through LoadObjData. The first HBlank handler writes story-screen plane/scroll values; the second writes a buffered VSRAM pair. The $40 is a fixed ROM span copied from after the length word, not a proof that each handler's executable body itself spans exactly $40 bytes.
